messages:
maya: Heads-up — thinking about a small spike to prototype SLO-shortfall driven routing + model-variant fallback behavior. need API shape + console preview.

maya: Problem statement: when a tenant's p99 crosses their tier SLO or availability drops, we should: 1) shift routing to lower-cost/safer variants, 2) throttle/burst to dedicated if available, 3) emit a clear telemetry reason so ops/console can show why fallback happened.

maya: Questions: what signals do we need in the policy API, how do circuit-breaker thresholds get specified (absolute vs relative), and what should the rollout/preview UX look like?

 aakash: Signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate (5xx), infra-availability (region up/down), and headroom (% of GPU slots free). cb thresholds should support both absolute (ms / %) and delta-from-baseline (e.g., +30% over baseline p99).

 aakash: Suggestion: expose both "static" thresholds in the tenant profile and an optional "adaptive" policy that uses short-window rolling stats. adaptive could be a multiplier on baseline to avoid noisy flips.

 samira: Telemetry needs: slo_trigger, cb_state (open/closed/half-open), fallback_variant, region, latency_ms, error_code, cost_estimate_tokens. We should tag events with tenant_id and rollout_id for correlation. Also surface sample traces where fallback happened.

 leon: Console UX: default "Simple" mode = single SLO slider per tier + toggle for auto-fallback. Advanced mode = JSON policy editor and simulated preview. The preview should show a short synthetic timeline and predicted % of traffic that would fallback at a given threshold.

 ops: How does this interact with quotas? e.g., if fallbacks push traffic to a lower-cost variant but that variant has a separate quota, we need deterministic preemption rules. Prefer: fallback only if target variant capacity > safe buffer or else preempt lowest-priority tenant traffic.

 maya: Proposed policy shape (rough):

```json
{
  "tenant_profile": "gold",
  "latency_slo_ms": 250,
  "availability_slo_pct": 99.9,
  "cb": {
    "metric": "p99_latency_ms",
    "mode": "delta",                // absolute | delta
    "threshold": 1.3,                // multiplier if mode==delta
    "window_seconds": 60,
    "min_samples": 50,
    "backoff_seconds": 300
  },
  "fallback_order": ["redwood-v2-8bit","redwood-v1-quant","hosted-small"],
  "fallback_guardrails": {
    "max_cost_increase_pct": 20,
    "require_region_compat": true
  }
}
```

 maya: Note: fallback_order is ordered by preference. fallback_guardrails prevents falling back to something that would exceed cost policy or break regional data constraints.

 aakash: Important: cache/KV compatibility between model variants. if we route to redwood-v1-quant but KV cache keys differ, latency may spike. need variant metadata: cache_schema_version and kv_compatibility flags. Router must consider compatibility when ordering fallbacks.

 samira: From telemetry side, emit an event when fallback happens with fields: "trigger_reason", "from_variant", "to_variant", "estimated_cost_delta", "tenant_tier", "cb_state_before". That lets Optimize and billing produce postmortems automatically.

 leon: For console preview, we should offer a /policy-simulate endpoint so UX can show a chart. e.g., POST /internal/policy-simulate with historical window + synthetic spike types -> returns percent fallback & estimated latency. policy-sim-bot could post a summary into channel.

 policy-sim-bot: deploy: policy-sim v0.1 deployed to staging. endpoint: POST /sim/v0/policy-eval

 ops: Rollout concern: can we do a staged rollout? e.g., enable SLO-shortfall routing on 5% of traffic for a tenant, evaluate telemetry, then 25%, etc. We need rollout_id in events. Also support automatic rollback if error-rate spikes after fallback.

 maya: yes — rollout plan: canary (5/25/100) + auto-rollback if fallback-induced error_rate increase > 2x baseline for 10m. We'll add rollout_id and canary_percent to the policy object.

 aakash: One more: circuit-breaker state machine must be observable and address noisy flips. Suggest: require N consecutive windows before opening, and a cooldown. The cb JSON above has backoff_seconds but add an "open_for_windows" param.

 samira: Dashboard: per-tenant card showing SLO health, current cb_state, active fallback_variant, and last_trigger_event (with link to sample traces). Also a tenant-level playbook link (runbooks) explaining steps to take.

 leon: For the UI: make the advanced editor validate compatibility (cache_schema_version mismatch warnings) and show cost delta estimates inline. Preview pane shows 3 synthetic scenarios: sudden latency spike, region outage, and steady degradation.

 maya: I'll prototype the policy JSON+simulator in a 2-week spike. volunteers? need someone from telemetry and Console.

 samira: I can pair on telemetry integration for the spike.

 leon: I'll take the Console preview component and mock graphs.

 aakash: I'll help wire the cb logic into the router and add KV-compat checks.

 ops: I'll write the rollout and quota interaction playbook.

 maya: Great. Setting up a short kickoff Friday 10am. I'll push a rough PR with the policy schema and a staging sim endpoint later today. :thumbsup:

 policy-sim-bot: test-run: sample sim for tenant t-342: predicted fallback 12% under 30% p99 delta, estimated cost change +7%.

 maya: thanks — will iterate on thresholds and guardrails in the PR.

 leon: +1 on canary steps. also add a "preview-as-tenant" switch so support can repro in console.

 samira: noted — will ensure telemetry includes rollout_id and preview_tag.

 maya: meeting invite sent.

 ops: ack.

 maya: closing thread for now — spike branch: github.com/redwood-inference/slo-routing-spike
